page: OVHcloud h200-1920-eph is a high-density, GPU-accelerated bare-metal instance powered by a KVM hypervisor. The system is equipped with 224 physical cores and 224 dedicated vCPUs from the AMD EPYC 9555 processor family running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Hardware multithreading is disabled, giving each dedicated vCPU an unshared physical core. System memory is scaled to 1920.0 GB of RAM, equating to 8.57 GB per core. The host includes 20,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network interface of 25 Gbps.

For massive parallel processing and AI acceleration, the server integrates an array of 8 NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs providing a combined total of 1128 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Benchmark measurements highlight its substantial compute capability, recording 470,347.59 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 3,672.92 in single-core performance, both placing in the top 10% tier. In language model inference workloads, it achieves 9,587.62 prompt tokens per second and 366.22 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, extending to 817.64 prompt tokens per second and 36.85 generation tokens per second on large 70B parameter models.

Data handling and memory operations demonstrate equivalent throughput, achieving 331.44 million Redis SET operations per second, 93.05 GB/s in static web serving, and 2,465.36 GB/s during multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. The combination of dense NVMe storage, vast GPU VRAM, and unconstrained physical cores delivers high resource concentration, trading off entry-level affordability for maximized throughput per host. These specifications make the instance best suited for large language model pre-training, fine-tuning, large-scale AI inference, high-performance computing (HPC), and massive real-time data processing pipelines.

The core accelerator subsystem features eight NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs delivering 1128 GB of combined VRAM. Network throughput is provisioned at 25 Gbps. Performance benchmarks confirm top-tier placement, yielding 470,347.59 in multi-core stress-ng tests and 331.44 million Redis operations per second. LLM inference capabilities scale effectively across model sizes, handling 817.64 prompt tokens per second and 36.85 text generation tokens per second on 70B models. This dense hardware deployment provides significant computing efficiency for large-scale AI training, distributed model serving, and compute-heavy scientific simulation workloads.
